analysis:
The change is documentation only: docs/developer/test.md bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a 'Focused Gemma 4 tensor-parallel checks' section (head lines ~1231-1345). No source, config, or runtime code changes. I examined the added test instructions against the threat model, especially TB-007 (inference engine), T-041 (prefix cache and SSD tier), and the TB-003 and TB-002 areas.

The new section describes synthetic-weight tests on one Mac over loopback. It covers prompt-prefix tiers and an SSD tier test: encrypted, owner-only records, refusal of stale, corrupted or other-key records, a daily write cap and a free-space floor. These match the T-041 posture (encrypted, HMAC-keyed, bounded) and do not weaken it. The section tells operators to use fresh scratch directories and explicitly disclaims real-weight numerics, pair qualification and speed, so it does not overclaim.

I found no instruction to disable a kill switch, use production cache roots or keys, or point tests at production. The ports 58123 and 58125 are loopback-only scratch values. The docs do not alter the TTL, adoption bound or scope derivation.

Remaining question: the described Gemma tensor-parallel runtime (a 'sealed local ring', collectives, prefix tiers across ranks) is a new code surface that is not in this batch. If it ships in the same PR, a later pass should review its authentication of ring peers, the T-041 cache-scope and salt handling across ranks, and any network exposure beyond loopback. This doc alone gives no evidence of a regression.
